context.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore is a scaled-down Amazon-style e-commerce platform for purchasing physical and electronic books with integrated reviews and recommendations. It delivers high scalability, security, and multi-region availability on AWS.

## Key Elements
* Customer and Admin / Content Manager (Human Actors)
* Online Bookstore (Core Software System)
* Payment Gateway (Stripe/PayPal)
* Shipping Provider APIs (FedEx/UPS)
* Tax & Compliance Service (Avalara)
* Recommendation Engine (AWS Personalize)

## Relationships
* Customer to Online Bookstore via HTTPS / TLS 1.3 (Web/Mobile App)
* Admin to Online Bookstore via HTTPS / TLS 1.3 with MFA and OAuth 2.0 / OIDC
* Online Bookstore to Payment Gateway via HTTPS/REST
* Online Bookstore to Shipping Provider APIs via HTTPS/REST
* Online Bookstore to Tax & Compliance Service via HTTPS/REST
* Online Bookstore to Recommendation Engine via HTTPS/REST with pseudonymized IDs

## Technology Stack
* AWS (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1): Multi-region cloud infrastructure ensuring 99.95% uptime and low latency
* AWS API Gateway: Mediates and secures all external egress points and traffic
* Web Application Firewall (WAF): Deployed at the edge for OWASP Top-10 mitigation
* TLS 1.3: Enforced for all external communications to secure data in transit
* OAuth 2.0 / OIDC: Standardized token-based session management for customer authentication

## Rationale
This architecture uses multi-region AWS deployment and edge security to guarantee 99.95% uptime and performance for 1M MAU. Decoupling third-party services via TLS 1.3 secured API gateways ensures strict GDPR/CCPA compliance and data protection.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[An Amazon-style e-commerce online bookstore built on AWS, designed to handle 1M MAU while ensuring GDPR and CCPA compliance.]
## Key Elements
[• Customers and Admins (Users)
• Single-Page Application (SPA) & Back-Office Admin Portal (React, Amazon S3, Amazon CloudFront)
• API Gateway (Amazon API Gateway)
• Core Microservices (Catalog & Search, Checkout & Order, Recommendation, Admin & Compliance via Spring Boot & Python/FastAPI on Amazon ECS Fargate)
• Data Persistence (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon DynamoDB)
• External Systems (Payment Gateway, Shipping Provider APIs, Tax & Compliance Service, Recommendation Engine)]
## Relationships
[• Users access SPAs via HTTPS over Amazon CloudFront
• SPAs communicate with API Gateway using REST/HTTPS and JWT authentication
• API Gateway routes traffic to ECS Fargate containers via VPC Links with mTLS
• Core services sync with external APIs (Payment, Shipping, Tax, Recommendations) using REST/TLS
• Services read/write to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon DynamoDB]
## Technology Stack
[• Frontend: React on Amazon S3 and CloudFront for sub-2s global page loads
• Backend: Spring Boot and Python/FastAPI on Amazon ECS Fargate for scalability and modularity
• Databases: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL for relational transactional data; Amazon DynamoDB for low-latency cart states
• Security & Networking: AWS KMS, AWS Secrets Manager, Amazon CloudWatch, and IAM for strict zero-trust isolation and compliance]
## Rationale
[This multi-tier container architecture on AWS isolates critical checkout and catalog workloads to guarantee high availability and sub-2-second performance. Dedicated administrative and compliance services ensure strict adherence to GDPR and CCPA regulations without impacting high-throughput customer journeys.]

Single-Page Application (SPA) & Back-Off.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore provides a global, scalable e-commerce platform for physical and electronic books with recommendations and reviews. It utilizes a React-based Single-Page Application and Back-Office Admin Portal deployed on AWS to deliver high-performance, secure user experiences.

## Key Elements
- Customer
- Admin / Content Manager
- Single-Page Application (SPA) & Back-Office Admin Portal (React, Amazon S3, Amazon CloudFront)
- Storefront Module (React, Redux Toolkit, DOMPurify)
- Admin Portal Module (React, React Router)
- Auth & Consent Manager (React Context, AWS Amplify, AWS Cognito)
- API Client Interceptor (Axios)
- Amazon API Gateway

## Relationships
- Customer -> Single-Page Application (SPA) & Back-Office Admin Portal: Accesses storefront via HTTPS over CloudFront [HTTPS]
- Admin / Content Manager -> Single-Page Application (SPA) & Back-Office Admin Portal: Accesses admin portal via HTTPS with MFA [HTTPS, OIDC/AWS Cognito]
- Storefront Module & Admin Portal Module -> API Gateway: Communicates via centralized Axios interceptor [REST/HTTPS, JWT]

## Technology Stack
- React: Powers component-based UI for high performance on 3G networks
- Amazon CloudFront & Amazon S3: CDN and object storage for sub-2s global page loads and strict Content Security Policy enforcement
- AWS Amplify & AWS Cognito: Manages OIDC authentication, JWT sessions, and MFA enforcement
- Redux Toolkit: Manages state for shopping cart optimistic updates and localized multi-currency rendering
- DOMPurify: Sanitizes user-generated customer reviews against DOM-based XSS

## Rationale
This architecture separates public storefront and administrative bundles across distinct S3 buckets to eliminate privilege leakage risks. Furthermore, it implements strict token management and client-side sanitization to satisfy OWASP Top-10 security and GDPR/CCPA compliance at scale.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore is a secure, high-performance, multi-region e-commerce platform designed to support 1 million monthly active users with 99.95% uptime. It enables customers and administrators to browse catalogues, securely checkout, write reviews, and receive recommendations while complying with GDPR and CCPA.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Customer, Admin / Content Manager
- **External Systems**: Payment Gateway, Shipping Provider APIs, Tax & Compliance Service, Recommendation Engine
- **Containers**: React SPA & Admin Portal, Amazon API Gateway, Core Microservices (Spring Boot, Python/FastAPI on AWS ECS Fargate), Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon DynamoDB
- **API Gateway Components**: AWS WAF, Authentication & Authorization Component, Rate Limiting & Throttling Component, Geographic Routing & Compliance Component, Routing & Protocol Translation Component
- **Security & Infrastructure**: AWS Secrets Manager, AWS CloudWatch, AWS X-Ray

## Relationships
- **React SPA** -> **AWS WAF**: Sends ingress HTTP/HTTPS traffic [HTTPS]
- **AWS WAF** -> **Authentication & Authorization Component**: Inspects traffic for OWASP Top-10 threats [HTTPS]
- **Authentication & Authorization** -> **Geographic Routing Component**: Forwards authenticated requests with validated JWTs [Internal]
- **Geographic Routing Component** -> **Core Microservices**: Routes traffic across regional VPC Links [mTLS, gRPC]
- **API Gateway** -> **AWS CloudWatch & AWS X-Ray**: Emits telemetry, metrics, and distributed traces [Internal]

## Technology Stack
- **Amazon API Gateway**: Acts as the scalable entry point for routing, rate limiting, and analytics.
- **AWS WAF**: Provides edge-level OWASP Top-10 mitigations, SQL injection, and XSS protection.
- **Amazon ECS Fargate**: Hosts containerized core microservices built with Spring Boot and Python/FastAPI.
- **AWS Secrets Manager**: Dynamically injects and rotates mTLS certificates, API keys, and signing secrets.
- **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL & DynamoDB**: Manages persistent transactional data and scalable NoSQL storage.

## Rationale
This architecture uses Amazon API Gateway combined with AWS WAF and edge-level authentication to instantly drop unauthorized traffic, ensuring high availability (99.95%) and strict security (OWASP Top-10) for 1M MAU. Multi-region deployments (`us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, `ap-southeast-1`) with geographic routing guarantee low-latency page loads (<2s) and full GDPR and CCPA compliance.

Core Microservices.analysis:
## Overview
[The Online Bookstore is a scaled-down Amazon-style e-commerce site for purchasing physical and electronic books with recommendations and reviews, designed to handle 1M MAU.]
[It is built on AWS across multiple regions, ensuring GDPR and CCPA compliance, multi-currency support, and 99.95% uptime.]

## Key Elements
*   **Customers & Admins**: End users and content managers interacting with the system.
*   **Frontend**: Single-Page Application (SPA) and Back-Office Admin Portal (React, Amazon S3, Amazon CloudFront).
*   **API Gateway**: Amazon API Gateway routing traffic via VPC Links [mTLS].
*   **Core Microservices Container**: Hosted on Amazon ECS Fargate, comprising:
    *   *Catalog & Search Component* (Spring Boot)
    *   *Checkout & Order Component* (Spring Boot)
    *   *Admin & Compliance Component* (Python/FastAPI)
    *   *Async Notification Service* (Python/FastAPI)
*   **Databases & Messaging**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon EventBridge, Amazon SNS, Amazon SES.
*   **External Systems**: Payment Gateway, Shipping Provider APIs, Tax & Compliance Service, Recommendation Engine.

## Relationships
*   API Gateway -> Core Microservices: Routes traffic [mTLS over VPC Links]
*   Core Microservices -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Reads/writes relational data [JDBC/TLS]
*   Core Microservices -> Amazon DynamoDB: Reads/writes cart states [AWS SDK / TLS]
*   Core Microservices -> Amazon EventBridge: Publishes/consumes domain events [AWS SDK / TLS]
*   Core Microservices -> Payment Gateway, Shipping Provider APIs, Tax & Compliance Service, Recommendation Engine: Processes transactions, fulfillment, compliance, and recommendations [REST/TLS]
*   Async Notification Service -> Amazon SNS / Amazon SES: Dispatches notifications [AWS SDK/TLS]

## Technology Stack
*   **Frontend**: React deployed on Amazon S3 and distributed via Amazon CloudFront for fast global performance (<2s on 3G).
*   **Compute**: Amazon ECS Fargate for serverless container orchestration of microservices.
*   **Languages & Frameworks**: Spring Boot for Catalog/Checkout; Python/FastAPI for Admin and Async Notification services.
*   **Databases**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL for relational data with AWS KMS encryption; Amazon DynamoDB for low-latency cart states.
*   **Messaging & Integration**: Amazon EventBridge for event-driven workflows; Amazon SNS/SES for asynchronous notifications.

## Rationale
[This microservices architecture isolates critical revenue-generating workflows like checkout from non-critical paths like recommendations to guarantee 99.95% availability and high scalability.]
[Event-driven patterns and managed AWS services ensure secure, asynchronous operations that easily scale to support 1M MAU while meeting strict GDPR and CCPA compliance standards.]

Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.analysis:
## Overview
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL serves as the primary relational database for the Online Bookstore, ensuring transactional integrity for shopping carts and secure checkouts.
- It provides scalable, highly available data storage across multiple global regions while enforcing strict GDPR and CCPA compliance.

## Key Elements
- Aurora PostgreSQL Cluster (Multi-AZ with Primary Writer and Read Replicas)
- Aurora Global Database (cross-region replication for us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1)
- Aurora Distributed Storage (auto-scaling up to 128TB across 3 AZs)
- PostgreSQL Extension Manager (`pg_stat_statements`, `pgcrypto`)
- IAM & Secrets Manager Integration
- Private Database Subnets (isolated VPC deployment)

## Relationships
- Core Microservices -> Aurora PostgreSQL Cluster: Executes queries and transactions [PostgreSQL wire protocol over TLS 1.3 via PgBouncer]
- Core Microservices -> IAM & Secrets Manager: Authenticates and manages database credentials [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
- Aurora PostgreSQL Cluster -> Amazon CloudWatch: Streams audit logs for compliance monitoring [AWS Internal API]
- Aurora PostgreSQL Cluster -> Amazon S3: Performs continuous backups and point-in-time recovery (PITR) with immutable storage [AWS Internal API]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Chosen for high availability, ACID compliance, and multi-region replication.
- AWS IAM & Secrets Manager: Implemented to eliminate static credentials and secure database access.
- PgBouncer: Utilized for connection pooling to sustain 1M MAU concurrency.
- AWS KMS: Applied for transparent data encryption (TDE) at rest and column-level PII encryption.

## Rationale
- The multi-AZ cluster and global database replication fulfill the 99.95% uptime and multi-region scalability requirements under heavy traffic.
- Strict network isolation, IAM authentication, and encryption mechanisms ensure comprehensive GDPR, CCPA, and OWASP Top-10 security compliance.

Amazon DynamoDB.analysis:
## Overview
An Amazon DynamoDB data layer for the Online Bookstore manages shopping carts, user sessions, and browsing history with low-latency access. It ensures secure, high-performance data operations globally across multiple regions.

## Key Elements
* Shopping Cart Table (`CartTable`)
* Session & History Table (`UserActivityTable`)
* DynamoDB Streams (`ActivityStream`)
* Global Tables Replicator
* DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)

## Relationships
* Core Microservices -> `CartTable` & `UserActivityTable`: CRUD operations via AWS SDK (HTTPS/TLS 1.3)
* `ActivityStream` -> Core Microservices / Recommendation Engine: Event consumption via Amazon Kinesis Adapter / AWS Lambda
* `CartTable` & `UserActivityTable` <-> Global Tables Replicator: Active-active multi-region replication via AWS backbone (Proprietary Protocol)
* Core Microservices -> DAX: In-memory read queries via AWS DAX SDK (TLS 1.3)

## Technology Stack
* Amazon DynamoDB: NoSQL database selected for predictable single-digit millisecond latency (R-02, R-06)
* AWS KMS: Customer-managed keys (CMK) with automatic rotation for encryption at rest
* DynamoDB Time-to-Live (TTL): Configured for 7-14 days to support GDPR/CCPA data minimization
* DynamoDB Global Tables: Multi-region replication in `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, and `ap-southeast-1` for 99.95% availability (R-07)
* DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX): In-memory caching for sub-millisecond read queries on user activity

## Rationale
This architecture uses DynamoDB to handle high-velocity cart and session data for 1M MAU without violating the 2-second page load limit. Comprehensive security controls, multi-region replication, and automated recovery ensure strict regulatory compliance and business continuity.
